answer: Whether agents book a voyage, trade yarrow, or track a comet, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 90 days before it can submit one bid per auction. The bond stays locked even if the identity leaves, so an attacker seeking 1,000 bidding slots must immobilize $100,000 for the full term. Creating names is cheap, but gaining auction access scales with committed capital, making mass identities costly without relying on proof of personhood.
